results.text:
Back to building in public. Rule: post weekly, only with numbers or decisions. No motivation threads.

Started a new SaaS with a co-founder. Boring bet: existing paying market, narrow niche, win on distribution and acquisition rather than product innovation. Goal is $20k MRR before anything fancy.

What happened in 4 days:

Tested 40 keywords in Google Keyword Planner (US + Canada). Top bids 2 to 40 CHF, nothing under the ~1.8 CHF max CPC the unit economics allow. Ads are for demand testing, not the acquisition engine.

Checked SERPs on 50 long-tail queries across 5 ideas. Fresh sites (<12 mo) rank everywhere on '[X] alternative' and vertical pages. SEO is winnable.

Selected idea: Missed call to automated text-back for US contractors (plumbers, roofers, HVAC). Search up +900% YoY, CPC 3 to 6 CHF, vertical SERPs empty.

Shipped http://keepthejob.com: 1 button, Stripe, $79/mo. Zero demos, zero calls, fully automated.

If nobody pays, just kill it and post the numbers here.

results.text:
BUILD IN PUBLIC – J1
Salut, moi c’est Paul. J’ai 24 ans.

J’ai lancé 5 SaaS ces dernières années.
💀 2 gros flops 
💸 2 sont montés à 3K et 5K de MRR
🚀 1 sur lequel j’ai bossé tourne aujourd’hui à +30K MRR

Mais ça… c’est la version LinkedIn.

La vérité ?
On a fait quasiment toutes les erreurs imaginables.
Des mois à coder avant de parler à un seul utilisateur.
Des features inutiles.
Des pivots sans vraie vision.

Et surtout, on a oublié une règle simple :

👉 Ton produit peut être top,
mais s’il est invisible, il ne vaut rien.

📸 Voilà à quoi ça ressemble. Une bonne idée… qui meurt dans l’ombre.

Aujourd’hui, je repars de zéro.
Pas de plan parfait. Pas de storytelling bullshit.
Juste moi, mon ordi, et l’envie de faire mieux.
En public. Brut. Sans filtre.

C’est parti.
#buildinpublic

results.text:
A multi-agent system is basically several specialized AI workers coordinated around one objective.

The important part: they are usually not truly independent “AI employees.” In practice, most multi-agent systems are an orchestration layer around multiple LLM calls, tools, memory, and shared state.

Each agent usually has its own role, instructions, available tools, and context.

For example, imagine an agency operations system.

A client submits:

“I need a website for my plumbing company and want more leads.”

Your system might run like this:

A supervisor agent receives the request and decides what needs to happen.
A research agent checks the business, competitors, location, services, and website.
A sales agent determines the likely service package, pricing range, and upsells.
A technical agent determines the required stack, integrations, hosting, and development effort.
A proposal agent combines everything into a proposal.
A reviewer agent checks the proposal for mistakes, contradictions, or missing information.
The supervisor returns the final result.

The agents communicate through structured data rather than just chatting randomly.

“Uses AI” is becoming a meaningless requirement for engineers.

The useful question is:

Does AI increase their output without increasing the team’s risk?

An AI-native engineer should still be able to:

→ understand unfamiliar code
→ challenge bad requirements
→ debug production issues
→ review generated code
→ make architecture decisions
→ take ownership of outcomes

Typing prompts faster isn’t engineering leverage.
Better judgment at higher speed is.

results.text:
The Pakistan Medical and Dental Council's decision requiring Afghan medical students in Pakistan to return to Afghanistan is patently discriminatory and arbitrary in nature. The consequences of this decision are especially severe for female students, many of whom have already been denied access to higher education in Afghanistan amid Taliban’s ongoing gender persecution and now face the prospect of losing one of the few remaining pathways to pursue their education and profession. Many of these students will have devoted years studying medicine, only to see their education brought to an abrupt and unjustifiable end, with little prospect of being able to resume their studies elsewhere.
 
Pakistan has obligations under international human rights law to uphold the right to education without discrimination on the basis of national origin. Amnesty International urges the authorities to adopt a humane and practical solution that allows Afghan students, including women and girls, to complete their education.
